materials.basis: Each glass is modelled from the printed nd and Abbe number: a two-term Cauchy curve through (nd, Vd), then a three-term Sellmeier with fixed poles fitted to it over the stated band. The model index is scaled by 1.0002772, the engine's air index at the d line, so that the index ratio at a glass-air surface is the printed nd.

approximations.description: The publication states nd and Vd only. A two-term Cauchy curve is solved exactly from those two values and a three-term Sellmeier with fixed poles is fitted to it. The relative index at the reference wavelength is the source's nd; the dispersion curve is a model.

The semi-diameters in the Project are derived, not transcribed: each is the larger of the traced axial marginal and field-edge chief-ray heights at the printed f-number and half field with a 2 % margin, reduced where the element geometry does not admit it. No clear-aperture value is taken from the publication.

The engine treats a model glass as an absolute refractive index and a gap as air at 20 C and 101325 Pa (n = 1.0002772 at the d line), so the ratio it uses at a glass-air surface is nd / 1.0002772. The model glasses are fitted to nd * 1.0002772 to make that ratio the printed nd.
The publication states the f-number but not the stop diameter. The modelled stop opening is solved so that the paraxial marginal ray reproduces the printed f-number.

evidence_notes: Engine paraxial EFL 10.556039 mm against the source's printed 10.56 mm.
Engine paraxial back focal length 41.099433 mm against the source's printed 41.1 mm.
The engine values and the printed values disagree beyond the intake tolerance.
